body: THE GOOD NUMBER: in FY18 Yes Bank reported ROE 17.7%, RoA 1.6% and gross NPA 1.28% (down from 1.72% the previous quarter) with loans up ~54%, numbers that rivalled HDFC Bank and earned a premium valuation; the stock peaked ~Rs 393-404 in Aug 2018. WHY IT LIED: ROE in a bank equals reported profit after provisions; under-provisioning lifts it. RBI's own inspections found NPA divergence of ~Rs 4,177 cr (FY16) and ~Rs 6,355 cr (FY17), i.e., reported NPAs were a fraction of real ones, and these divergences were publicly disclosed in 2017. A 54% loan growth rate in a corporate book is evergreening risk, and the lending was concentrated in groups that later failed (ADAG, Essel, DHFL, IL&FS, Cox & Kings, Jet). Low-cost deposits (CASA) were thin, so the bank paid up for bulk money. Sep 2018: RBI refused to extend the founder's term. GNPA went 1.3% (FY18) -> 7.4% (Sep 2019); moratorium Mar 2020; stock ~Rs 5.6. TEST: compare loan growth with system growth (3x system = red), read divergence notes, list top exposures by group, check CASA and cost of funds; ROA for a bank should be earned with granular retail, not by lending to stressed promoters. LESSON: a high ROE is a result, not a quality; in lenders the denominator of risk shows up 2-3 years later. Contrast HDFC Bank, whose ROE came with low-cost deposits and seasoned retail assets.

data.good_number: FY18 ROE 17.7%, RoA 1.6%, GNPA 1.28%, loan growth 54%, premium P/B
data.test_that_catches_it: RBI divergence disclosures; loan growth >30%/yr in corporate book; CASA ratio; exposure to stressed groups; regulator action on CEO
data.why_misleading: NPAs were under-recognised (RBI divergence Rs 4,177 cr FY16, Rs 6,355 cr FY17); growth came from corporate loans to stressed groups

title: Hidden trap: Yes Bank's 17.7% ROE and 1.28% gross NPA
